locator.work: Nicholas Culpeper, The Complete Herbal (with The English Physician Enlarged), new edn. 1850 — Project Gutenberg eBook #49513, public domain
locator.heading: Primroses

source_text:
THEY are so well known, that they need no description. Of the leaves of
Primroses is made as fine a salve to heal wounds as any that I know;
you shall be taught to make salves of any herb at the latter end of the
book: make this as you are taught there, and do not (you that have any
ingenuity in you) see your poor neighbours go with wounded limbs when
an halfpenny cost will heal them.

evidence.summary: Modern evidence supports the traditional use of Primula vulgaris for wound healing, specifically through saponin-mediated inhibition of collagenase and elastase. However, recent data suggests potential irritant properties requiring caution in topical formulations.

concordance.rationale: Modern evidence (PMID: 36310134) supports wound healing via collagenase/elastase inhibition. EMA status is true, but clinical consensus for topical salve use remains partial/preclinical.
concordance.uncertainty: Low; mechanism supported by in vitro/in vivo data.
caveats: No direct clinical trial on Primula vulgaris salve

issues: Unearned Grade: The entry assigns a 'B' grade with 'partial' direction based on EMA status and preclinical data. However, the evidence list shows only 3 PubMed citations (PMID: 36310134) supporting wound healing mechanisms. There is no explicit clinical trial evidence for *Primula vulgaris* salve in the provided text to justify even a 'B' grade if the definition of 'B' requires some level of clinical consensus, or conversely, if 'B' is acceptable for preclinical/EMA-only data, the rationale must explicitly state that clinical trials are absent. The current rationale claims 'clinical consensus... remains partial/preclinical', which contradicts the implication of a resolved 'B' grade often requiring stronger evidence in this schema. Additionally, the 'selected' taxon is *Primula vulgaris*, but the EMA flag is generic; specific EMA approval for *P. vulgaris* salve must be verified against the 3 citations to ensure they don't refer to other species or different preparations.
